## Data Processing Part 2

### Import packages
```{r import-packages, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(here) 
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

### 1. Join with USREC data (recession indicator)
Join the 3 transformed CSV files on recession indicator values. 1 indicates a recession month, while 0 indicates non-recession month.

```{r merge-usrec, message=FALSE}

# Parse the date format "1959-01-01", setting the 1st of the month as floor in case
parse_month <- function(x) {
  floor_date(as.Date(parse_date_time(x, orders = "Ymd")), "month")
}

# Load USREC and standardise data types
usrec <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "USREC.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  rename(date = 1) %>%
  transmute(month = parse_month(date), USREC = as.integer(USREC))

# Join USREC on FRED MD transformed datasets
add_usrec <- function(file) {
  df <- read_csv(here("data", "processed", file), show_col_types = FALSE)
  date_col <- "sasdate"

  out <- df %>%
    mutate(month = parse_month(.data[[date_col]])) %>%
    left_join(usrec, by = "month") %>%
    select(-month)

  n_na <- sum(is.na(out$USREC))
  if (n_na > 0) warning(file, ": ", n_na, " rows have no matching USREC value")

  write_csv(out, here("data", "processed", sub("\\.csv$", "_usrec.csv", file)))
  out
}

files <- c("fred_md_macro_clean.csv",
           "fred_md_macro_financial_clean.csv")

merged <- setNames(lapply(files, add_usrec), files)

# Quick check: row counts and how many months are recessions
sapply(merged, function(d) c(rows = nrow(d), recession_months = sum(d$USREC, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

### 2. Missing data heatmap and table

This heatmap shows the availability of each predictor's data with time. It aims to give a board overview of data availability trends and continuity, to ensure that a sensible cut off can be made to handle missing values.

```{r missing-heatmap, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}

df <- read_csv(here("data", "processed", "fred_md_macro_financial_clean_usrec.csv"),
               show_col_types = FALSE)

predictors <- setdiff(names(df), c("sasdate", "USREC"))

miss_long <- df %>%
  mutate(yr = year(sasdate) + (month(sasdate) - 1) / 12) %>%  #change months to year + decimal
  select(yr, all_of(predictors)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-yr, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(status   = if_else(is.na(value), "Missing", "Available"),
         variable = factor(variable, levels = predictors))   # keep file's column order

cutoff_yr <- 1962   # reference line

ggplot(miss_long, aes(x = variable, y = yr, fill = status)) +
  geom_raster() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = cutoff_yr, colour = "#E63946", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Available = "#1D3557", Missing = "#F4A261")) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq(1960, 2025, by = 5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Data Availability by Predictor",
       x = "Predictors", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
        panel.grid   = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top",
        plot.title   = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
```

From the heatmap, most predictors are available in continuous chunks, from a certain date onwards. Some predictors are missing large chunks of data, and shall be removed from the analysis.


```{r missing-predictors, message=FALSE}
missing_summary <- tibble(
  variable    = predictors,
  n_missing   = sapply(predictors, function(v) sum(is.na(df[[v]]))),
  pct_missing = round(n_missing / nrow(df) * 100, 1),
  first_valid = sapply(predictors, function(v) as.character(min(df$sasdate[!is.na(df[[v]])]))),
  last_valid  = sapply(predictors, function(v) as.character(max(df$sasdate[!is.na(df[[v]])])))
) %>%
  filter(n_missing > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_missing))

knitr::kable(missing_summary,
             col.names = c("Variable", "Months missing", "% missing", "First valid", "Last valid"),
             align = "lrrcc")
```

Based on this summary, a sensible cut off point is from July 1962 onwards, where VIXCLSx is available. The first 4 predictors in the list (ACOGNO, UMCSENTx, TWEXAFEGSMTHx, ANDENOx) will be removed due to large amounts of missing values.


### 3. Drop relevant predictors and set cut off month

```{r trim-sample}
drop_vars  <- c("ACOGNO", "UMCSENTx", "TWEXAFEGSMTHx", "ANDENOx")
start_date <- as.Date("1962-07-01")

files_usrec <- sub("\\.csv$", "_usrec.csv", files)

# Load the merged files and drop the 4 predictors (any_of skips ones a file doesn't have)
dfs <- setNames(lapply(files_usrec, function(f) {
  read_csv(here("data", "processed", f), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    select(-any_of(drop_vars))
}), files_usrec)

# End date: the latest month where every remaining predictor, in every file, has data
end_date <- as.Date(min(sapply(dfs, function(d) {
  preds <- setdiff(names(d), c("sasdate", "USREC"))
  min(sapply(preds, function(v) max(d$sasdate[!is.na(d[[v]])])))
})), origin = "1970-01-01")

# Trim all three files to the same window
trimmed <- lapply(dfs, function(d) filter(d, sasdate >= start_date, sasdate <= end_date))

# Save
for (f in names(trimmed)) {
  write_csv(trimmed[[f]], here("data", "processed", sub("_usrec\\.csv$", "_final.csv", f)))
}

# Check
end_date
sapply(trimmed, function(d) c(
  rows             = nrow(d),
  predictors       = ncol(d) - 2,
  recession_months = sum(d$USREC),
  missing_cells    = sum(is.na(d))
))
```
